summary: Plan MHPSS assessments, referrals and monitoring for disaster response. Explore the five-day training and its practical exercises.
lede: Psychosocial impact training for disaster settings helps practitioners assess needs and coordinate safe, community-informed support. It is designed for MHPSS coordinators, programme officers and frontline workers who organize support and connect people with services as access and needs change. Participants practise needs and service mapping, Psychological First Aid and confidential referrals, then use monitoring to inform response planning.
audienceIntro: This course suits practitioners coordinating or delivering community and frontline psychosocial support, connecting people to services, or monitoring emergency activities. It also supports adjacent health, protection and education staff whose work requires clear MHPSS roles and referral links.

prerequisites: Intermediate-level practitioners should have prior exposure to community or frontline support, humanitarian or social services, or coordination of related activities. No coding or programming is required. Clinical assessment and treatment remain within the scope of appropriately qualified health-care providers.
